writeup: TIC 72729777 is a candidate eclipsing binary star identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 21.55 percent and an orbital period of 57.351087 days, with no secondary eclipse detected. The detection carries a high signal-to-noise ratio of 1480.3 in the Baylight Statistics analysis, and pixel-level imaging confirms the signal with a peak signal-to-noise of 53.2, though the centroid offset of 7.5 arcseconds warrants noting. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. However, a data quality flag indicates that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the true period is double the initial measurement - a pattern typical of certain eclipsing systems rather than an observational artifact.
